newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Jan 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Jan 10.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Friday's edition of The Wall Street Journal:
- Volkswagen AG agreed to pay General Motors $100 million and to buy $1 billion of GM parts over seven years to settle a civil suit alleging trade-secret theft.
- GM indicated it is exploring a public offering of a stake in its Delphi unit.
- Energy prices pushed the producer price index up 0.5 percent in December. Stock and bond prices rose on the reports.
- CSX and Conrail can block other suitors from acquiring Conrail for two years, according to decisions by regulators and a judge.
- Airline workers are increasingly demanding in contract talks, spurred by the industry's prosperity.
- Big retailers posted lukewarm December sales.
- The plan to sell the Hughes Electronics defense operations will require GM to make a huge bet on the prospects of the acquiring company.
- Fed governor Lawrence Lindsey notified the White House that he is resigning after five years on the board.
- Disney Chief Michael Eisner's contract was extended through September 2006.
- The Time Warner chairman said the entertainment giant's cash flow would increase at a "very solid double digit" rate this year.
- Comcast has won the right to buy control of E! Entertainment for $310 million from Time Warner.
- Iridium, a consortium of 17 companies, aims to launch the first three of a planned 66 satellite system as the group shifts its target audience to a richer and bigger market.
- Digital Equipment cut prices by up to 47 percent on servers and workstations based on its flagship Alpha chip.
- Motorola posted a 45 percent drop in quarterly profit.
- The chip industry remained on the path to recovery in December.
- Even under the optimistic assumption that Japanese corporate earnings will double in the next year, Japan's market is still 25 percent more expensive than the highflying Dow Jones industrials.
